text.title: ASP.NET Core Patterns Worked Examples
text.summary: Worked code examples for the controller, the service, and the global IExceptionHandler, followed by an end-to-end trace and the final artefact this methodology emits.

example.note: CancellationToken on every action (cancellation-token-threaded). No DbContext, no business logic (controller-calls-service-only). Returns a DTO, never an entity (record-dtos-at-boundary). Keyset cursor `after`, not Skip/Take (keyset-pagination).

TimeProvider injected for testable time (timeprovider-injected). CancellationToken on SaveChangesAsync / ToListAsync. AsNoTracking on the read (asnotracking-on-reads); eager .Include(), no lazy load (eager-include-no-lazy-loading). Returns DTOs, not entities.
One error contract for every path (problem-details-error-contract); the middleware order is the one middleware-order-authn-before-authz pins.
Two SaveChanges calls are not atomic together without the explicit transaction (explicit-transaction-multi-step-writes).

section.title: Trace
section.p: A feature applied end-to-end: controller→service→repository layering, scoped DbContext, CancellationToken on every async call, ProblemDetails errors from a single IExceptionHandler, record DTOs mapped at the boundary, TimeProvider for clock reads, AsNoTracking + eager .Include() on reads, keyset pagination on the list endpoint, an explicit transaction around the multi-step write, and WebApplicationFactory + Testcontainers Postgres for the integration suite.
